resources.string: Floating handle for full-screen zoom. Press and hold, then move to zoom in live. Double-tap to keep the zoom, then press the handle and move: the view follows your finger. Double-tap again to restore.
The handle is on screen. Tap it for quick settings. Can’t see it? Use “Bring back the handle” below.
Eye needs the accessibility permission to show the handle and zoom the screen.
The system lists Eye as on, but it isn’t running. It was probably stopped to save power. Turn Eye off and on again in Accessibility settings.
If the handle is lost or hidden, or the screen is stuck zoomed in, this puts everything back.
Handle restored. Look for the blinking blue ring.
Eye isn’t running yet. The saved handle position was cleared. Turn Eye on first.
Zoom level, fade, size and handle position go back to their defaults.
Many phones stop background apps to save power, and then the handle vanishes. Do all three:
Tries to open your phone maker’s auto-start page. If it can’t, it shows the manual steps for your phone.
Open the recent-apps screen and lock the Eye card. The way depends on your phone.
Run this once from a computer (phone connected, USB debugging on). After that, if the system stops Eye, opening this app turns it back on by itself.
Couldn’t open that page directly. Follow the steps shown.

• Tap: quick settings panel
• Drag: move the handle
• Press and hold, then move: zoom in live and the view follows your finger (speed = Follow sensitivity); let go to restore
• Double-tap: zoom in and keep it
• While zoomed: press the handle and move, same following; let go to keep the zoom
• Double-tap again: restore
• While you hold, the handle hides under your finger and reappears when you let go
Turn off the system’s own magnification (Accessibility → Magnification, and its shortcuts), or the two fight over your touches.

1. Tap “Open accessibility settings” below.
2. Find “Eye” (it may be under “Installed apps” or “Downloaded apps”).
3. Switch it on and confirm.
4. Switch greyed out, or a “restricted setting” message (Android 13 and up)? Tap “Allow restricted settings” below, then on the app info page tap ⋮ (top right) → “Allow restricted settings”, then repeat step 1.
5. Turn off the system’s own magnification, or the two fight over touches.

Back in Eye, the status turns green and the handle appears at the screen edge.
Keep Eye alive on your phone
Menu names differ slightly between system versions.
On any phone: Settings → Battery → Eye → No restrictions (or Unrestricted), and keep Eye’s auto-start switch on.
Xiaomi / Redmi / POCO: Settings → Apps → Manage apps → Eye → turn on Autostart and set Battery saver to No restrictions. In recent apps, pull the Eye card down (or long-press it) and tap the lock.

Huawei / Honor: Settings → Apps → App launch → Eye → turn off Manage automatically, then turn on Auto-launch, Secondary launch and Run in background. In recent apps, pull the Eye card down to lock it.

OPPO / realme / OnePlus: Settings → Apps → App management → Eye → turn on Auto-start and set Battery usage to Allow background activity. In recent apps, tap the card’s menu (or pull it down) and choose Lock.
vivo / iQOO: Settings → Battery → Background power consumption → Eye → Allow. Also i Manager → App manager → Autostart → Eye on. In recent apps, pull the Eye card down to lock it.
Samsung: Settings → Battery → Background usage limits → Never sleeping apps → add Eye. In recent apps, tap the Eye icon → Keep open.
Higher sensitivity: a small finger move travels farther, so you never need to reach the screen edge.
Switch off to hide the handle (Eye keeps running). Switch on to show it again.
Eye isn’t running yet. This will apply once it is turned on.
